word:hebrew:H1046.explanation: This word refers to the place-name “Beth Pelet,” rather than describing an action, quality, or person. It identifies a settlement mentioned in the Old Testament, appearing four times in two verses: twice in Joshua 15:27 and twice in Nehemiah 11:26. The name is preserved in English as “Beth Pelet.” Without the surrounding verse text, its precise role in each passage cannot be expanded beyond identifying this location.

word:hebrew:H1103.explanation: Balas means to pinch sycamore figs, a process necessary to ripen them.

word:hebrew:H1280.explanation: Beriyach means a bolt or bar.

word:hebrew:H1338.explanation: This Hebrew word is a proper name rendered “Bithron,” referring to a specific place rather than expressing an action, quality, or general object. It occurs only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 2 Samuel 2:29. Because the surrounding verse text is not available here, its precise geographical significance cannot be stated beyond identifying it as the named place Bithron.

word:hebrew:H1374.explanation: Gebim is a name rather than a general word describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, and its English rendering is “Gebim.” Its grammatical function is to identify a particular place or named location in the sentence, though the available verse information does not supply a fuller description of that location. The word occurs only in Isaiah 10:31.

word:hebrew:H1451.explanation: Gederite means an inhabitant of Geder.

word:hebrew:H1507.explanation: Gezer is the name of a place in Palestine.

word:hebrew:H153.explanation: Edra means arm and can figuratively refer to power or force.

word:hebrew:H1635.explanation: Gerem means a bone. It is used for bones that lions broke into pieces among those cast into the den.

word:hebrew:H1640.explanation: Gâraph means to bear off violently—to sweep away.

word:hebrew:H1716.explanation: Dagar means to brood over eggs or young.

word:hebrew:H1899.explanation: Hegeh means a muttering or sound. It can also describe mourning or a tale.

word:hebrew:H1914.explanation: Hiddai is a personal name, used to identify an individual rather than to express an action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 2 Samuel 23:30. English renderings preserve the name as “Hiddai,” so the available information supports recognizing it as a proper name without assigning it an additional meaning or translating it as an ordinary descriptive word.

word:hebrew:H1958.explanation: This Hebrew word expresses “woe,” serving as a forceful cry of distress or warning. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Ezekiel 2:10. Because it appears only once and no verse text is provided here, its precise force in that sentence depends on the surrounding passage. Its role is connected with what was written and revealed in Ezekiel’s vision, but its central lexical sense remains a solemn declaration of “woe.”

word:hebrew:H2018.explanation: This rare Hebrew term refers to something mentioned in Genesis 19:29, but its precise meaning cannot be established from the lexical information available here. It occurs only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in that verse, and no explicit definition or approved meaning term is provided. Its surrounding relationships connect it with God and the events named in the verse, but without the verse text, those connections do not justify a more specific explanation.

word:hebrew:H214.explanation: Otsar means a depository or storehouse where treasures are kept.

word:hebrew:H2177.explanation: Zan means a kind or sort, including different kinds.

word:hebrew:H2252.explanation: “Habaiah” is a personal name, referring to an individual or family designation rather than expressing an action or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs twice, once in Ezra and once in Nehemiah. The same name appears in both passages, showing its use as an identifying name. Its precise role in either verse depends on the surrounding passage and the person or family being listed there.

word:hebrew:H2371.explanation: Chazael is the name of a king of Syria.

word:hebrew:H2393.explanation: Chezqah means prevailing power. It can also describe strength or being strong.

word:hebrew:H2502.explanation: Chalats means to pull off or remove, and it can also mean to deliver. In battle settings, it describes people equipped or armed for war.

word:hebrew:H258.explanation: Achad means to unify or collect one's thoughts. It can also express going one way or the other.

word:hebrew:H2663.explanation: Haphraim is a proper name, rendered “Haphraim,” rather than a common word describing an action, quality, or object. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Joshua 19:19, so its meaning cannot be expanded into a broader everyday definition from this record. In ordinary Bible reading, treat it as a named term whose precise significance depends on the surrounding passage, not as a word with a descriptive definition.

word:hebrew:H2766.explanation: Chârim is the name of an Israelite, rendered Harim in English.

word:hebrew:H2843.explanation: This word refers to a person called a “Hushathite.” It functions as a personal designation rather than describing an action, quality, or object. The Hebrew Old Testament uses it five times, and each occurrence is rendered “Hushathite.” It appears in passages naming or identifying individuals in the historical records of David’s mighty men and officials. The word’s precise significance in any one passage depends on the surrounding verse, but its basic sense is the identification of someone as a Hushathite.

word:hebrew:H2968.explanation: Yâ’ab means to desire or long for something.

word:hebrew:H2986.explanation: Yabal means to bring, carry, or lead.

word:hebrew:H3000.explanation: Jeberechiah is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, and its English rendering is “Jeberechiah.” The available lexical information does not provide a separate descriptive definition for the name, so its ordinary sense is simply the person identified by this name. It appears in Isaiah 8:2; understanding that verse’s specific role requires the surrounding text.

word:hebrew:H3075.explanation: This Hebrew word is a personal name, rendered “Jehozabad,” rather than a common word describing an action or quality. It identifies people named Jehozabad in four Old Testament occurrences, appearing in Kings and Chronicles. The name functions as a proper designation for a person, so its significance comes from whom the passage names, not from an abstract concept. Its precise reference is determined by the individual passage in which it appears.

word:hebrew:H3156.explanation: This word is a personal name, rendered “Izrahiah.” It identifies an individual rather than describing an object, action, or quality. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs three times, in two verses: twice in 1 Chronicles 7:3 and once in Nehemiah 12:42. Because it is a name, its basic function is to identify the person who bears it; the surrounding verse supplies that person’s role or situation.

word:hebrew:H3211.explanation: Yalid means born. It can describe someone born in a household, in contrast with someone bought with money from a foreigner.

word:hebrew:H3372.explanation: Yare means to fear or be afraid. It can also mean to revere Yahweh, with fearing him joined to keeping his commandments.

word:hebrew:H3404.explanation: Yᵉrîyâh is a personal name, rendered Jeriah or Jerijah, identifying an Israelite among the sons of Hebron.

word:hebrew:H3448.explanation: Yishay is the personal name rendered Jesse. He is identified as David’s father.

word:hebrew:H3541.explanation: Kôh means thus or like this, showing how something is done. It can also point to a place as here or to a time as now.

word:hebrew:H3633.explanation: Kalkôl is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H3790.explanation: Kethab means to write. It is used for writing a letter and setting down a dream.

word:hebrew:H3912.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to “Letushim,” a name preserved in the genealogy of Abraham’s descendants. It functions as a name identifying a particular group in the biblical record, rather than describing an action, quality, or object. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at Genesis 25:3, in a birth-and-genealogy setting. The available English renderings retain it as “Letushim,” so the name itself is the clearest meaning.

word:hebrew:H399.explanation: Akal means to accuse, eat, or devour. It can describe bringing an accusation. It also describes eating, such as eating grass. It can also describe devouring much flesh.

word:hebrew:H4104.explanation: Mehuman is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or general concept. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, in Esther 1:10, and the English rendering preserves it as “Mehuman.” Because it functions as a name, its meaning is primarily identification: it distinguishes this person from others in the account. The name itself does not provide enough information to describe the person’s character or role without the surrounding verse and passage.

word:hebrew:H4148.explanation: Mûwçâr means instruction or discipline. It can also refer to chastisement or reproof.

word:hebrew:H4290.explanation: Machtereth means a burglary or breaking in. It can also mean a secret search.

word:hebrew:H4333.explanation: Mishael is a Hebrew personal name, not a word that describes an action, quality, or object. In the Old Testament Hebrew corpus represented here, it appears once, in Daniel 2:17, and the English rendering preserves it as “Mishael.” Because a personal name is being carried over rather than translated into an ordinary descriptive term, its role is to identify a particular person; the surrounding verse is needed to identify that person’s place in the passage.

word:hebrew:H4456.explanation: Malqowsh means the spring rain, also called the latter rain.

word:hebrew:H4500.explanation: Manor means a beam, especially a weaver’s beam.

word:hebrew:H4539.explanation: Masak means a cover or veil. It can refer to a hanging used at a tent or court entrance.

word:hebrew:H4575.explanation: Maʻadannah means a bond or group. It can also be rendered as “influences.”

word:hebrew:H4672.explanation: Matsa means to find or acquire. It can also indicate that something exists or is present, as when no helper is found.

word:hebrew:H4711.explanation: Matsats means to suck or draw out milk.

word:hebrew:H485.explanation: Alummah means a sheaf, something bound together.

word:hebrew:H4867.explanation: Mishbar means a breaker of the sea, a billow, or a wave.

word:hebrew:H4913.explanation: Mashal refers to a person identified by the name “Mashal,” rather than expressing a general action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in 1 Chronicles 6:74, and the name is preserved as “Mashal” in the available English renderings. Because no verse text or explanatory definition is available here, the safest understanding is simply that this word functions as a personal name in that occurrence.

word:hebrew:H5006.explanation: Na’ats means to scorn or despise.

word:hebrew:H5187.explanation: This Hebrew word means “bear,” referring to the animal. It appears only once in the Old Testament, in Zephaniah 1:11, so its normal meaning is supported by a single occurrence rather than by a broad range of passages. The word is associated there with the surrounding wording of that verse, but the verse text is not available here for further explanation. Its basic lexical sense remains “bear.”

word:hebrew:H5334.explanation: Nezib is a Hebrew name rendered “Nezib.” It identifies a specific named entity rather than expressing an action, quality, or general idea. In the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, it occurs once, at Joshua 15:43, and the English renderings preserve it as a name rather than translating it into an ordinary descriptive word. The available wording does not provide enough context to explain more about the entity itself, so its clearest lexical sense is simply the proper name Nezib.

word:hebrew:H5378.explanation: Nâshâ means to lend on interest. It can also mean to press someone for a debt owed.

word:hebrew:H5396.explanation: This Hebrew word means “breath.” It refers to the breath or life-giving air associated with a living person. The word appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Daniel 5:23, so its wider range of use cannot be established from repeated biblical examples. Its precise force in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic sense is the breath that sustains physical life.

word:hebrew:H5428.explanation: Nathash means to tear away. It can describe plucking a people from their land or pulling something up by its roots.

word:hebrew:H5464.explanation: Sagrîd means pouring rain—very rainy conditions.

word:hebrew:H5561.explanation: Sam means an aroma associated with sweet spices.

word:hebrew:H5583.explanation: This Hebrew word expresses helping: giving assistance or support to someone. In its only recorded Old Testament occurrence, it describes an action rather than a person, place, or object. Its English rendering is “helping,” so its central idea is active assistance. It appears once in the Hebrew Bible, in Ezra 5:2; the surrounding verse is needed to explain exactly who is helping and how. The word itself does not establish the full circumstances without that context.

word:hebrew:H5617.explanation: Sepharvaim is the name of a city.

word:hebrew:H562.explanation: Omer means a word. It can also mean speech, a promise, or a thing.

word:hebrew:H5709.explanation: Adah means to alter. It can also describe departing or passing away, or removing or taking something away.

word:hebrew:H5730.explanation: Eden means pleasure. It is also used as the name of a place.

word:hebrew:H5745.explanation: Obal is a personal name, referring to an individual rather than expressing an action, quality, or object. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Genesis 10:28, and is rendered “Obal.” Because the available passage information does not include the verse text or surrounding context, the name’s particular role in that genealogy cannot be explained further here. Its basic meaning is therefore its identifying function as the name of a person.

word:hebrew:H5842.explanation: Et means a stylus or marking stick. It is used as a pen for writing and engraving.

word:hebrew:H5910.explanation: Accho is the name of a place. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it appears once, in Judges 1:31, and is rendered “Accho.” Because this word is a place-name rather than a common noun or action word, its meaning is primarily the identification of that location. The surrounding verse determines what is being said about Accho, but the word itself functions as a geographical name. Its recorded use is limited to that single occurrence.

word:hebrew:H5965.explanation: ʻAlas means to leap for joy or exult. It can also mean to wave joyously.

word:hebrew:H6014.explanation: ʻAmar means to gather grain, including binding it into sheaves. It can also mean making merchandise of a person.

word:hebrew:H6058.explanation: Aneph means branching or full of branches.

word:hebrew:H6199.explanation: Ar'ar means naked, figuratively describing someone poor or destitute.

word:hebrew:H621.explanation: This Hebrew word is the personal name “Asenath,” identifying a woman rather than expressing an action, quality, or general object. It appears three times in the Old Testament, all in Genesis, where it functions as a person’s name in accounts involving family and genealogy. Its use remains consistent throughout its occurrences: it refers to Asenath herself. The surrounding passage supplies the particular details about her role, while the word’s ordinary meaning is simply this proper name.

word:hebrew:H6227.explanation: Ashan means smoke. For example, it describes smoke rising from a city. It can also be used figuratively when days are compared to smoke.

word:hebrew:H6292.explanation: Piggul means fetid. Figuratively, it can describe something ceremonially unclean.

word:hebrew:H6421.explanation: Pelaliah is a Hebrew personal name, referring to an individual rather than describing an action, quality, or object. Its ordinary English rendering is “Pelaliah.” This name appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, in Nehemiah 11:12. Since no broader lexical definition or additional occurrences are provided, its meaning as a personal name cannot be expanded beyond identifying the person called Pelaliah. The surrounding verse is needed to explain that individual’s role in the passage.

word:hebrew:H6515.explanation: Paruah is a Hebrew personal name, preserved as “Paruah” rather than translated into an ordinary descriptive word. It appears once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 1 Kings 4:17. Because it functions as a name, its meaning for readers is primarily identification: it identifies a particular person rather than expressing an action, quality, or idea. The surrounding verse supplies the information needed to understand that person’s role there.

word:hebrew:H6559.explanation: This Hebrew word is a proper name, rendered “Perazim.” It identifies a specific name rather than expressing an ordinary action, quality, or object. The word occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Isaiah 28:21, so its precise significance there depends on the surrounding verse and passage. Its capitalization in the rendering reflects its function as a name, not a general vocabulary term. Scripture’s use of it is therefore tightly limited to that single occurrence.

word:hebrew:H6560.explanation: Perets-Uzza is the name of a place, rendered “Perezuzza” in the KJV.

word:hebrew:H6685.explanation: Tsowm means a fast or fasting.

word:hebrew:H6762.explanation: Tselaʻ is a place in Palestine, rendered as Zelah in English.

word:hebrew:H6803.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “pot,” referring to a container or vessel. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in Exodus 16:33, and functions there as an object connected with speech, taking, placing, and giving. The available scriptural pattern presents it as something used to hold or preserve an item, rather than as an action or quality. Its precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage, but its basic meaning is a pot or container.

word:hebrew:H6946.explanation: Kadesh is the name of a place in the desert.

word:hebrew:H7013.explanation: This Hebrew noun means “spear,” referring to a weapon used as an object in the sentence. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, at 2 Samuel 21:16. The available wording identifies the object but does not provide enough surrounding verse text here to explain the specific action or significance attached to it. Its role is therefore best understood simply as naming a spear within that passage.

word:hebrew:H715.explanation: Ardon is the name of an Israelite.

word:hebrew:H7167.explanation: Qara means to tear or rend.

word:hebrew:H7376.explanation: Râṭâsh means to dash down or dash in pieces.

word:hebrew:H7398.explanation: Rekuwb means a vehicle used for riding, including a chariot.

word:hebrew:H7431.explanation: Remes means a reptile or other rapidly moving animal. Scripture uses the word for creatures that creep on the ground.

word:hebrew:H7512.explanation: Rᵉphaç means to stamp, pressing something down with the feet.

word:hebrew:H759.explanation: Armon means a citadel or fortified stronghold. It can also refer to a palace.

word:hebrew:H7637.explanation: This Hebrew word means “seventh,” identifying something that comes in position seven within an ordered sequence. It is used for a numbered day, time, person, or other item, helping mark its place in relation to what comes before and after it. The word appears 98 times in the Hebrew Old Testament, from Genesis through Zechariah, showing regular use for identifying the seventh position. Its exact significance in any verse depends on the surrounding passage.

word:hebrew:H7682.explanation: Sagab means to be high or set on high; it can also describe being made safe or strong.

word:hebrew:H7725.explanation: Shuwb means to turn back or return. It can also mark something happening again, as in coming again.

word:hebrew:H7750.explanation: Sûwṭ means to turn aside or become wayward. It describes those who turn aside to lies.

word:hebrew:H7769.explanation: Shuwa means a halloo or cry. It can also refer to riches.

word:hebrew:H7804.explanation: Shezab means to set free or deliver.

word:hebrew:H7848.explanation: Shittah means acacia. Its wood was used for boards, poles, and altars.

word:hebrew:H7941.explanation: Shekar means an intoxicating strong drink.

word:hebrew:H8063.explanation: The word refers to a “mantle,” functioning as a noun for something worn or used as a covering. In the Hebrew Old Testament, it occurs once, at Judges 4:18. Because no verse text is provided here, its precise appearance and significance in that scene must be determined from the surrounding passage rather than from the word alone. The available rendering identifies the object simply as a mantle, without supplying a broader range of meanings.

word:hebrew:H8081.explanation: Shemen means oil, especially a liquid oil. It can also refer to anointing oil.

word:hebrew:H8166.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to goats. It appears twice in the Hebrew Old Testament corpus, both times in Leviticus, where it identifies the animal being presented in the sacrificial instructions. The ordinary meaning is therefore a goat or goats, with the exact number determined by the sentence in which it appears. Its two recorded occurrences are Leviticus 4:28 and 5:6.

word:hebrew:H8188.explanation: This Hebrew word is rendered “Seorim” and functions as a name rather than a translated descriptive term. It occurs once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 1 Chronicles 24:8, and the English renderings preserve the name in that form. Since no explanatory definition or verse text is available here, its basic lexical sense is best stated simply: Seorim is a biblical name. Its precise role in that passage depends on the surrounding context.

word:hebrew:H8302.explanation: Shiryown means a coat of mail, a kind of protective armor.

word:hebrew:H838.explanation: Ashur means a step or going.

word:hebrew:H8452.explanation: Torah means a custom. It can also describe a manner, as in “the manner of man.”

word:hebrew:H8571.explanation: This Hebrew word means “tip.” It is used as a noun for the end or extremity of something. In its eight Old Testament occurrences, it appears in Exodus and Leviticus, especially in passages involving ritual actions. The word itself identifies the particular tip being addressed, while the surrounding passage determines its exact physical reference and significance. Its occurrences are concentrated in these priestly and cleansing instructions rather than spread broadly across the Old Testament.

word:hebrew:H8593.explanation: Ta'ar means a razor. It can also mean a scabbard.

word:hebrew:H8618.explanation: Teqowmem means an opponent—one who rises up.

word:hebrew:H8654.explanation: This Hebrew word refers to the “Tirathites,” the name used for a particular group of people. It appears only once in the Hebrew Old Testament, in 1 Chronicles 2:55. Because no short definition or broader usage is available, its clear meaning is limited to this group designation rather than a general action, quality, or object. The word’s precise significance in that verse depends on the surrounding passage and the identity of the people named there.

word:hebrew:H874.explanation: This Hebrew verb expresses making something “plain”—presenting words or instruction so they are clear and understandable. It functions as an action word rather than a name for a person, object, or quality. In the Old Testament, it occurs three times, including passages in Deuteronomy and Habakkuk. Its repeated association with communicated words or instruction supports the idea of making what is expressed plain. The surrounding passage determines exactly what is being made plain in each occurrence.

word:hebrew:H980.explanation: Bachurim is a place in Palestine.
